bib.title: Aligning Text-to-Image Models using Human Feedback

question: Can human feedback on generated images be used to fine-tune a text-to-image model so its outputs follow prompts (count, color, background) more faithfully, and what design choices govern the alignment-fidelity tradeoff?
hypothesis: Fine-tuning with a reward function learned from binary human feedback improves image-text alignment over the pre-trained model; naive fine-tuning is expected to hurt fidelity unless regularised with diverse data.
contributions: A simple fine-tuning method for aligning a text-to-image model using human feedback.
Human evaluation shows up to 47% improvement in image-text alignment at the expense of mildly degraded fidelity.
The learned reward predicts human assessments better than CLIP score; rejection sampling on it also improves alignment.
Naive fine-tuning with human feedback reduces fidelity; design choices matter for the alignment-fidelity tradeoff.

method.summary: Stable Diffusion v1.5 images are generated for templated prompts (count, color, background, combinations) and labelled good/bad by humans. A CLIP-embedding MLP reward is trained with MSE plus an auxiliary prompt-classification loss. The diffusion module is then fine-tuned by reward-weighted likelihood (a supervised, not PPO, update) with a pre-training-data regulariser.
method.task: text-to-image alignment via learned reward from human feedback (reward-weighted likelihood fine-tuning)

datasets.name: Human-labelled image-text set (Stable Diffusion samples)
datasets.size: 27528 image-text pairs; 2700 prompts in main text (2774 in Appendix B); up to 60 images per prompt (60 or 6 by category)
datasets.source: generated by SD v1.5; labelled by two human labelers (binary good/bad, skip allowed); feedback class-balanced
datasets.preprocessing: Skipped queries not used. Labelers see three images per prompt. Table 2 feedback: Good 46.5%, Bad 48.5%, Skip 5.0%.

datasets.name: Unlabeled generated images
datasets.source: extra SD v1.5 samples on the same prompts

datasets.name: LAION-5B aesthetic subset (improved_aesthetics_6.5plus)
datasets.source: LAION-5B filtered by aesthetic score predictor
datasets.preprocessing: used for the pre-training loss term

datasets.name: MS-COCO val2014
datasets.preprocessing: one random caption per image; images resized to 256x256 for FID

datasets.name: Evaluation prompts
datasets.source: Table 4; unseen = objects absent from human dataset (bear, tiger, rabbit, rose, wolf)

models.name: Stable Diffusion v1.5
models.architecture: latent diffusion; CLIP language encoder frozen, only diffusion module fine-tuned

models.name: Reward model
models.architecture: ViT-L/14 CLIP embeddings of image and text concatenated into two-layer MLP, 1024 hidden each, ReLU, sigmoid output

training.objective: Reward: L = L_MSE + lambda * L_pc (prompt-classification cross-entropy over softmax of r/T). Generator: L(theta) = E_Dmodel[-r(x,z) log p(x|z)] + beta * E_Dpre[-log p(x|z)].
training.optimizer: AdamW (beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, eps=1e-8) for fine-tuning; reward optimizer not stated
training.batch_size: 512 total (256 pre-training data, 256 model-generated), per-GPU 8 on 4 GPUs
training.regularisation: pre-training-data NLL term weighted by beta (beta value not stated)

other.online_RL: not used; PPO/KL-regularised RLHF deferred to future work

inference.decoding: Stable Diffusion sampling; settings not stated
inference.samples: Rejection sampling: 16 images per prompt, best 4 by reward kept, compared to 4 random images; human eval compares sets of 4 images
inference.prompting: templated prompts, e.g. 'Two green dogs on the table.'

metrics.name: Human image-text alignment / fidelity preference
metrics.definition: 9 independent raters per query pick better set or tie; report % of queries by number of positive votes, highlighting >=7/9 (two-thirds)

metrics.name: Reward preference accuracy
metrics.definition: for two images from the same prompt, whether r(x1,z)>r(x2,z) when raters prefer x1; compared with CLIP score

metrics.name: FID on MS-COCO
metrics.definition: pytorch-fid between generated and real val2014 images at 256x256

baselines: Fine-tuning ablations without unlabeled / pre-training data
eval.protocol: Human raters, 9 per query, 120 prompts; no seeds or significance tests reported; per-category mean +/- std in Tables 5-7.

evidence.quote: From a set of 2700 English prompts

results.claim: 50% of fine-tuned-model samples get at least two-thirds of rater votes for better image-text alignment than original Stable Diffusion.
results.setup: Fine-tuned SD v1.5 vs original, 60 seen + 60 unseen prompts, human raters.
results.quote: 50% of samples from our model receive at least two-thirds vote (7 or more positive votes) for image-text alignment
results.note: Figure 4 labels read 50%, 3%, 10%; the 3% is the original model's win share read from the figure layout, inferred.

results.claim: Fine-tuning degrades fidelity: 15% of queries favour the original at two-thirds vote versus 10% favouring the fine-tuned model.
results.quote: fine-tuning somewhat degrades image fidelity (15% compared to 10%)
results.note: Which side each number belongs to is read from the sentence and Fig 4, not stated explicitly.

results.claim: Learned reward predicts human preferences on unseen prompts at about 80%, better than CLIP score.
results.setup: Held-out images, unseen text prompts; CLIP score as baseline; value read approximately from text.
results.quote: its performance on unseen text prompts (∼80%)
results.note: CLIP score accuracy is only in Fig 3a, not in text.

results.claim: Rejection sampling (best 4 of 16 by reward) gets 46% two-thirds votes for alignment without losing fidelity.
results.setup: Original SD + reward rejection sampling vs 4 random images.
results.quote: (46% with two-thirds preference vote by raters)

results.claim: Against rejection sampling, the fine-tuned model gains 10 points of alignment but loses 17 points of fidelity.
results.quote: achieves a 10% gain in image-text alignment (20%-10% two-thirds vote) but sacriﬁces 17% in image ﬁdelity (3%-20% two-thirds vote)

results.claim: Fine-tuning on human-labelled data alone nearly doubles FID (13.97 to 26.59) while raising reward 0.43 to 0.69; adding unlabeled and pre-training data restores FID to 16.76 at reward 0.79.
results.setup: Ablation of data used in Eq. 2.
results.table: Table 3, rows Original model, Fine-tuned model w.o unlabeled & pre-train, w.o pre-train, Fine-tuned model; FID 13.97, 26.59, 21.02, 16.76; reward 0.43, 0.69, 0.79, 0.79
results.note: Caption mentions CLIP scores but none are tabulated.

results.claim: Halving the training images per prompt lowers reward accuracy on seen and unseen prompts; the prompt-classification auxiliary loss improves it.
results.setup: Training data 11K vs 23K; with/without PC loss; numbers only in Fig 3.
results.quote: model accuracy decreases on both seen and unseen prompts as data size decreases

results.claim: Feedback was good 46.5%, bad 48.5%, skip 5.0% over 27528 images; SD is worst at counts (34.4% good) and combinations (35.8%), best at color (70.4%).
results.setup: Human labels on SD v1.5 outputs.

limits: Authors: oversaturated colors, duplicated entities and lower diversity appear in some fine-tuned outputs.
Authors: human data covers only count, color, background with binary feedback; larger, diverse data and ranking feedback are future work.
Authors: no RL (PPO) or KL regularisation used; they believe RLHF may do better but defer it.
Reward accuracy on unseen prompts is only about 80%.
Only one base model (SD v1.5), two labelers for training data, no seeds or significance tests, no learning rate or beta/N values, no code or data release stated.
Fidelity loss explanations (alignment-focused feedback, limited diversity, small pre-training subset) are expectations, not tested.
